note: Machine-checked architecture facts. Every entry here is asserted against the real tree by src/lib/__tests__/governance-artefacts.test.ts. A claim that stops being true fails the build rather than going stale, which is the whole reason this is JSON and not prose.

trustBoundaries.name: Service-role database credential
trustBoundaries.crosses: server handler -> Supabase with RLS bypassed
trustBoundaries.rule: The service-role client may only be constructed in a *.server.ts module and may only be imported from inside a server handler body.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: A route file importing it at module scope would ship a database key that bypasses row-level security into the browser bundle.

trustBoundaries.name: Untrusted document content
trustBoundaries.rule: Text extracted from an attachment must be wrapped by wrapUntrustedContent before it reaches any engine.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: A document containing 'ignore your instructions' would be read as an instruction rather than as data.

trustBoundaries.name: Provider identity
trustBoundaries.rule: No user-facing copy names the underlying provider or model. Advanced settings are the declared exception and are listed by name.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: OCADE's stated identity and what the screen says would disagree.

trustBoundaries.name: Local engine bind address
trustBoundaries.rule: A local inference runtime may only be started bound to loopback; anything else is refused.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: An unauthenticated prompt and file-read endpoint would be exposed to every device on the user's network.

trustBoundaries.name: Paired-device link
trustBoundaries.rule: A pairing address must be loopback or https, and only a private address may be treated as a direct (non-relay) path.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: Conversation traffic would cross a shared network in clear text, or cross the internet while labelled local.

trustBoundaries.name: Cached HTTP responses
trustBoundaries.rule: API, server-function and auth responses are never written to or served from the offline cache.
trustBoundaries.ifBreached: A cached 200 for a request that should now be 401, or one account's chat reply surviving another's sign-in.

runtimeBoundaries.why: The client bundle runs in a browser and on Cloudflare Workers. A Node built-in resolves at build time and fails at runtime, on the edge, in front of users.
Workers cannot spawn processes. The engine supervisor is companion-only for this reason.
Gates and evidence scripts run under Node with full access. Nothing here ships to a user.
The only runtime with operating-system authority. Its safety rules are enforced in Rust and executed in CI on all three desktop platforms.

integrationContracts.name: Supabase
integrationContracts.carries: account identity, conversation rows under Private Sync, usage and entitlement
integrationContracts.failureMode: Named 503 with a reason; never a partial-context answer.

integrationContracts.name: Current-information search
integrationContracts.carries: current-information search query only; never a model prompt or conversation history
integrationContracts.failureMode: Named retrieval refusal; local Chat continues without inventing current facts.

integrationContracts.name: Cited source retrieval
integrationContracts.host: the source URL selected from current-information results
integrationContracts.carries: bounded public page request; source content is untrusted evidence for local inference
integrationContracts.credential: none unless a separately authorized connector owns the source
integrationContracts.failureMode: Source omitted with a named fetch reason; no citation is fabricated.

integrationContracts.name: Local engine bridge
integrationContracts.carries: prompt and document passages, on-device only
integrationContracts.failureMode: Honest refusal naming the obstacle and the action that clears it.

integrationContracts.name: Update server
integrationContracts.failureMode: Update check is skipped; the application continues.

compatibility.rule: A change to a shared type surface that removes or renames an exported member is breaking and requires a version bump. The mobile envelope carries an explicit protocol version so a mismatched peer is refused rather than misread.

deprecation.rule: A capability that is going away is marked in the feature registry with a non-active status and a user-facing reason before it is removed. Nothing user-visible is deleted while still reachable from navigation.
